questions.question: Which formula states the triangle inequality for real numbers?

options: The size of a sum is at least the sum of the sizes.
Absolute value always turns sums into products.
The size of a sum is at most the sum of the sizes.
Every absolute value inequality must be strict.

questions.question: Which statement is a common equality case for real numbers?
options: Equality can hold when $x$ and $y$ have the same sign.
Equality holds only when $x$ and $y$ have opposite signs.

questions.question: Which conclusion follows from $|x-y|\le |x|+|y|$?
options: The distance between $x$ and $y$ is bounded by the sum of their distances from $0$.
The distance between $x$ and $y$ is always equal to $|x|+|y|$, no matter which values are selected.
